product.amstrad-pc1512.summary: 8 MHz 8086 desktop with 512–640 KB, integrated planar 640×200×16 graphics, proprietary keyboard and mouse, RTC, serial, parallel and one or two 360 KB floppy drives.
product.amstrad-pc1512.history: Introduced in 1986, the PC1512 combined an 8086, monitor, mouse and a substantial software bundle at a disruptive price. SD and DD denoted one- and two-floppy systems; HD10 and HD20 added factory hard-disk packages while retaining the same main platform.
product.amstrad-pc1512.warning: PARTIAL EMULATION: diskless SD/DD configurations are close to grade B and have broad direct tests. HD10 uses an explicitly compatible IBM/Xebec ST-506 profile rather than the original Xebec Owl/SASI adapter; HD20 remains unavailable. Keyboard electronics, physical light-pen triggering and phase-dependent video contention are still approximate or incomplete.
PC1512 SD — one 360 KB floppy, no hard disk
PC1512 DD — two 360 KB floppies, no hard disk
PC1512 HD10 — compatible 10 MB hard-disk profile
PC1512 HD20 — original controller not yet identified
product.amstrad-pc1512.creation.firmware: v1 ROS + 40078 character ROM — available legacy approximation
product.amstrad-pc1512.creation.note: The memory selector represents LK4 and the documented 32 KB expansion populations. BIOS language and character-ROM selections expose LK1–LK3 and LK6–LK7. LK5 and LK8 are not offered because their behavior is not sufficiently implemented.
product.amstrad-pc1512.creation.hdnote: HD10 is behavior-compatible, not a claim of original controller fidelity. HD20 remains visible but unavailable until its Xebec/Tandon controller and firmware are established.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.commerc: SD had one 360 KB floppy, DD had two, and HD10/HD20 combined one floppy with 10 or 20 MB hard-disk packages. PC-CM colour and PC-MM monochrome monitor bundles were sold.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.accesso: Optional 8087-2, 128 KB RAM expansion, second floppy, hard-disk kits, mouse, joystick, light pen and three 8-bit expansion slots.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.cpu: Intel 8086-2 at 8 MHz in maximum mode, with a 16-bit onboard memory bus and a 4 MHz 8-bit peripheral/expansion bus.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.memory: 512 KB parity RAM is fitted on the main board. Up to 128 KB can occupy 80000h–9FFFFh in 32 KB blocks, giving validated totals of 512, 544, 576, 608 and 640 KB.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.video: The integrated VDU provides CGA-like text/graphics plus proprietary planar 640×200×16, a 16 KB CPU aperture, fixed CRTC behavior, light-pen registers and documented 12–46-clock display-memory contention.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.floppy: Onboard uPD765-compatible controller for at most two 5.25-inch 360 KB drives. BluMach specializes drive selection, motor/DMA gating and rejects impossible drive 2/3 selectors.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.storage: The optional historical adapters are unresolved. The selectable HD10 compatibility profile uses an IBM/Xebec 1985 option ROM and 306/4/17 MFM image; it passes INT 13h write/read but is not the observed Owl/SASI adapter.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.interfa: Onboard 8250 COM1 at 3F8h/IRQ4, Centronics parallel at 378h/IRQ7, proprietary serial keyboard, quadrature mouse counters at 78h/7Ah and a light-pen header.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.rtc: HD146818-compatible RTC/NVR at 70h/71h with IRQ2; direct NVR access and periodic interrupt routing pass tests.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.firmwar: Selectable v1, v2 and v3 ROS/character-ROM pairings are defined by filename. Only the local legacy v1 ROS plus later 40078 character ROM is currently available and tested; no ROM bytes ship with BluMach.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.jumpers: LK1–LK3 select BIOS language/diagnostics, LK4 represents memory population, and LK6–LK7 select the character-ROM quadrant. LK5 ROM decode and LK8 floppy READY behavior are documented or inferred but not exposed as unsupported controls.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.verifie: Direct tests cover all RAM totals, planar video and VDU registers, light-pen software registers, floppy boot/read/write and drive 1, COM1 loopback/IRQ4, RTC IRQ2, keyboard reset/ACK, mouse counters, parity/I/OCHCK, reset and compatible HD10 I/O. DOS regressions remain stable.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.emulati: Partial (grade C; diskless SD/DD configurations are close to B). The machine-specific model covers the 8 MHz 8086, 512–640 KB, integrated planar video, keyboard and mouse interfaces, RTC, COM1, parallel port, reset and up to two floppy drives. HD10 is a compatible profile rather than an exact controller; HD20 is unavailable.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.lineage: The original PC1512 emulation was created in PCem and subsequently maintained in 86Box. BluMach preserves that foundation and its reusable device cores; this revision evolves it with corrections derived from the manuals and direct tests.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.blumach: Corrected the 16 KB video aperture, planar writes and fixed VDU registers; keyboard reset/ACK, wrapping mouse counters, RTC IRQ2, board-wide reset, parity/I/OCHCK and floppy gating/drive selection. Added PC1512-owned COM1, all RAM populations, firmware/language/character-ROM/monitor controls, the two-drive UI limit and SD/DD/compatible-HD10 creation profiles.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.limitat: Still approximate or pending: phase-dependent 12–46-clock video contention; execution of the 40042 keyboard MCU and serial timing; physical light-pen triggering; mouse scaling, phases and button timing; bit-parity RAM and natural I/OCHCK; full parallel-port coverage; READY/LK8, FDC reset timing and media edge cases; coherent ROM-set and PC-MM tests. The original HD10 and HD20 controllers remain unemulated.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.referen: Amstrad PC1512 Technical Reference Manual: hardware, firmware-visible interfaces and programming model.
product.amstrad-pc1512.technical.service: Amstrad PC1512 PC-MM/PC-CM Service Manual: schematics, monitor variants and hard-disk kit information.
